Context: Fortinbras: Go softly on.
Captain: They are of Norway, sir.
Captain: Against some part of Poland.
Captain: The nephew to old Norway, Fortinbras.
Hamlet: Goes it against the main of Poland, sir, Or for some frontier?

Hamlet: Whither wilt thou lead me? Speak. I'll go no further.

Polonius: Look whe'er he has not turned his color and has tears in 's eyes. Prithee, no more.
Polonius: My lord, I will use them according to their desert.
Polonius: Come, sirs.
First Player: Ay, my lord.
Hamlet: We'll ha 't tomorrow night. You could, for a need, study a speech of some dozen or sixteen lines, which I would set down and insert in 't, could you not?

What sayest though?

Fine. A speech for some twenty lines, perhaps, with good sense and heart; then leave it there. But mark well this—speech must be built upon truth, else it is only empty art. And yet, what shall speak better than I? For many a man hath been a villain once when angry, or in love once mad—but I have oft kept my self honest enough even whilst I lay in a stinking bed. To thee, dear Polonius, if I were a villager—for heaven forbid that name—I'd think of robbing your daughter from her father and holding her captive until she marries one of my choosing! Nay, I am too much accustomed to the ways of courtiership, where a little flattery and a few paltry favors can win most hearts. So pray, friend, what do ye think should be done? What course dost thou advise me to pursue?</|system| <|reflexive|>I wonder how they look now, knowing they've spoken such things.
